page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-80xCPU-512GB is a high-density instance in the Cloud Native family configured with 80 x86_64 vCPUs and 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding 6.4 GB of RAM per core. The underlying compute infrastructure is powered by AMD EPYC 9354 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on a KVM hypervisor. Hardware instruction set support includes AVX-512 extensions (F, VNNI, BF16) along with AES, VAES, and SHA cryptographic accelerators. The instance features no local storage and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring reliance on external block storage and separately provisioned networking.

Benchmark data reflects high multi-core compute throughput and raw memory bandwidth. The instance achieves a top-tier stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 194,997.67 and a PassMark CPU score of 101,132.81, supported by top-tier performance in PassMark CPU extended instructions (153,384.96) and encryption tests (101,656.62). Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 402.44 GB/sec for large-block reads and 218.77 GB/sec for writes. Similarly, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 793.93 GB/sec and Redis SET operations hit 143.15 million operations per second, both scoring in the top 10% tier.

Performance profiles exhibit distinct tradeoffs between multi-core scaling and serial operations. While Geekbench software compilation with Clang (61,944.0) and ray tracing (104,664.0) place in the top decile, single-threaded metrics such as gzip compression (29.77 GB/sec) and the PassMark memory score (2,499.89) sit in the average category. Furthermore, LLM text generation is constrained without discrete accelerators; generating tokens on a 7B model performs in the bottom 25% at 7.79 tokens per second, despite strong prompt processing at 2,523.66 tokens per second on smaller 135M models.

With a 1:6.4 core-to-memory ratio and high core counts, the configuration delivers strong resource density for distributed memory caches, in-memory databases, large-scale software builds, and multi-threaded data transformations. Environments relying on dense core parallelism and high throughput memory access will realize optimal efficiency, provided workloads do not require direct local disk storage or hardware-accelerated deep learning inference.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-80xCPU-512GB is an AMD EPYC 9354-powered virtual server featuring 80 x86_64 vCPUs and 512.0 GB of RAM on a KVM hypervisor. Delivering a ratio of 6.4 GB per core, the configuration supports AVX-512 instructions (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration. It includes no bundled local storage, no GPUs, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional multi-threaded performance, with stress-ng multi-core (194,997.67), PassMark CPU (101,132.81), and uncached memory bandwidth (402.44 GB/sec read) placing in the top 10%. Tradeoffs appear in modest single-core throughput and limited generative AI text processing capabilities. The server is well positioned for memory-intensive caching systems like Redis, parallel CI/CD compilation, and large-scale data processing.
